Triaged #102 against executable source: the reported guard is the `if (!code)` presence check at line 44 and the reported sensitive action is verifySignedOAuthState(stateRaw, user.id) at line 59. Every path to the token exchange (line 78) and to the organization_social_integrations upsert (line 167) passes the fail-closed `if (!signed)` block at lines 60-63. The user-controlled `code` narrows the paths that reach the sensitive action rather than widening it, and no attacker-supplied value can skip the HMAC check. Not exploitable; no code change is warranted and inventing one would be a behaviour change without a defect.

Triaged #94: the sink is createHmac('sha256', <test secret>) in a vitest file that never ships, and the value is a fixed test-only literal. A keyed HMAC is a MAC, not a password hash. Not exploitable; registered as a governance record rather than silenced in code.
